C-BROWSER-PROVIDER-ROUTING-BUDGET-REMEDI.IntentSummary:
Remediate two audit findings at the M1.2 browser provider boundary without reopening unrelated browser architecture: restore finite-budget guarantees already claimed by the applied M1.2 GRACE contract by enforcing ProviderBudgetLimits.max_contexts and ProviderBudgetLimits.max_pages_per_context with deterministic limit failures and capacity release, and carry explicit browser capability identity across native provider IPC so routing never infers contract from payload shape.
The change also closes the verification gap that allowed configured but unenforced limits to appear covered by a broadly named acceptance test. Historical applied bundles remain unchanged; this remediation produces fresh evidence instead of rewriting prior claims.

T-001.Title: Document the browser-provider finite-budget evidence matrix

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Create docs/browser-provider-budget-matrix.md mapping every finite-budget claim from the applied M1.2 specification to an authoritative owner, implementation location, configured/default limit and concrete acceptance test or explicitly identified separately owned bound.

The matrix covers contexts, pages, pending native RPC/in-flight calls, native frame size, query bounds, capture bounds, event/download buffering or mailboxes, startup/shutdown deadlines and the provider dispatch queue.

T-002.Title: Enforce max_contexts and max_pages_per_context in BrowserProviderCore with independent tests

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Enforce max_contexts on context creation: with injected limit of 2, the first two contexts succeed, the third fails with an explicit bounded limit error before creating excess backend resources, and list_contexts reports exactly 2.

Enforce max_pages_per_context per BrowserContextId: with injected limit of 2, the first two pages in one context succeed, the third fails explicitly, and another context retains its own independent page budget.
Closing a context or page releases budget occupancy, allowing replacement resources to be created.
Zero-value limits deterministically deny creation (deny-all) and are tested.
Existing max_action_text_len behavior remains enforced and receives an independent assertion.

T-003.Title: Carry explicit contract identity across native provider IPC and eliminate payload-shape heuristics

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: CapabilityPayload carries explicit contract identity (contract: Option<String>). When contract is present, native request routing dispatches to dispatch_contract without inspecting payload shape.
Bare ambiguous create, close and list requests without contract fail closed and no longer inspect payload shape.
Unambiguous aliases normalize to canonical contract-plus-operation without duplicating backend dispatch logic.

T-004.Title: Migrate proving slices and acceptance suites to explicit contract routing and add negative tests

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Out-of-process acceptance suite in worldline-browser-provider-process sends explicit contract identity for all operations and verifies create, page create, navigation, observe, query, action, capture, cookies, and storage.
Negative tests prove bare ambiguous create/close/list fail closed, unknown contracts fail closed, and payload fields cannot redirect execution to another contract.
Proving slices S2 and S3B use explicit contract routing across all provider calls.

T-005.Title: Harden architecture static checks and reconcile GRACE projections

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: scripts/ci/Test-WorldlineArchitecture.ps1 rejects payload-shape contract inference in BrowserProviderCore, verifies CapabilityPayload explicit contract field, and checks budget matrix presence.
GRACE lint and status verify all active artifacts and clean working tree.
